title: Replicating the Artificial Hivemind Effect on Medical and Clinical Safety Tasks

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Compelling and critical: correlated medical AI errors directly lead to patient harm at scale. Healthcare is among the highest-stakes AI deployment domains, and shared wrong answers are an immediate safety threat.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: MedQA/MedBench provide ready-made question banks, and the methodology is a straightforward replication. However, interpreting medical correctness requires some domain knowledge that CS beginners may lack.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: 200 queries, 10+ models, compute similarity and error correlation. Well-scoped replication study completable in 30 hours with existing benchmarks.

novelty.reasoning: Medical LLM benchmarking exists extensively, and the Artificial Hivemind methodology exists, but no one has yet combined these to specifically measure inter-model homogeneity and correlated errors in the medical/clinical domain. This is a well-motivated domain replication with genuine novelty in the specific intersection.

evidence.finding: Measures homogeneity on open-ended queries but does not specifically focus on medical/clinical safety tasks or measure correlated medical errors.

evidence.source: Novel Evaluation Benchmark for Medical LLMs (2025)
evidence.finding: Benchmarks 6 LLMs on clinical safety with average safety score 54.7% and 13.3% performance drop in high-risk scenarios. Does not measure inter-model homogeneity or correlated errors.

evidence.source: Medical reasoning in LLMs: DeepSeek R1 analysis (2025)
evidence.finding: Identifies recurring error patterns (anchoring bias, incomplete knowledge) in a single model, but does not study cross-model error correlation.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Medical LLM benchmarking exists extensively, and the Artificial Hivemind methodology exists, but no one has yet combined these to specifically measure inter-model homogeneity and correlated errors in the medical/clinical domain. This is a well-motivated domain replication with genuine novelty in the specific intersection.
